title: Earth's Interior and Mantle Convection
seo_title: Earth's Interior Worksheets: Layers, Seismic Waves and Mantle Convection (Earth Science)
standard_text: Develop a model based on evidence of Earth's interior to describe the cycling of matter by thermal convection.
meta_desc: Free high school Earth and space science worksheets on Earth's interior (NGSS HS-ESS2-3): layers, density, P and S waves, the shadow zone, S–P lag and mantle convection. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Hot rock rises; cool rock sinks.
key_sub: Seismic waves reveal the layers; internal heat drives mantle convection.
body_html:
How to think about it

Earth's hot interior cycles rock by slow convection.

  • Layers: crust, mantle, liquid outer core, solid inner core. Lithosphere (rigid plates) sits on the softer asthenosphere.
  • Evidence: S waves cannot cross the liquid outer core (shadow zone); P waves bend; Earth is denser inside.
  • Heat from radioactive decay drives convection: hot rock rises, cool rock sinks, moving plates.
Example

S–P lag 30 s. Distance?

30 × 8

Answer: about 240 km

Example

Probe at 4,000 km depth?

Between 2,900 and 5,150 km

Answer: outer core

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the mantle is liquid lava.
  • Thinking S waves travel through the outer core.
  • Thinking the Sun drives mantle convection.

faq.q: How do we know what Earth's interior is like?
faq.a: Seismic waves change speed and direction at boundaries. S waves cannot pass through the liquid outer core, and Earth's high average density shows iron deep inside.
Hot, less dense rock rises slowly while cooler, denser rock sinks, cycling matter and helping to move tectonic plates.
Mostly radioactive decay of elements like uranium, thorium and potassium, plus heat left from Earth's formation.
